mainTopic: What the כהנים wore during the פייס, the layout of לשכת הגזית, and the jobs of the second פייס
overview: The גמרא continues the debate about what the כהנים wore during the פייס. רב נחמן says בגדי חול, and רב ששת says בגדי קודש. A משנה about removing the כהנים' clothes turns out to fit both views. רב ששת then brings a ברייתא in which the ממונה removes a מצנפת from a כהן's head. The גמרא rejects that proof, because a כהן can own a privately made priestly-style garment. From the same ברייתא, אביי proves that לשכת הגזית was half in קודש and half in חול, with one door to each side. A new משנה then lists the thirteen jobs given out by the second פייס, and בן עזאי gives a different order for bringing the limbs. The גמרא asks whether there was one draw or a separate draw for each job. A proof from 'four פייסות' is rejected, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to read the משנה as describing the lottery winners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה about removing the כהנים' clothes refers to those who won the פייס. That would mean they had been wearing בגדי חול, which supports רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about those who won the lottery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove רב נחמן's view from the משנה just quoted. It says the clothes being removed must belong to the winners of the פייס, so those clothes were בגדי חול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהנים' clothes were taken off and only the מכנסים were left on. If this describes the winners getting ready for the עבודה, then what they wore during the פייס must have been בגדי חול. That would be a challenge to רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that…?' — a formula used to suggest a reading that proves a point
The lottery used to assign the Temple services among the כהנים
Who won (who were chosen)

phrases.english: What, is it not about those who won the lottery?
phrases.notes: This would mean their בגדי חול were removed so they could put on בגדי קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה cited on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that the פייס was done in בגדי חול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה stating that the clothes were removed and only the מכנסים were left on

steps.title: רב ששת: the משנה describes those who lost
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the משנה describes the כהנים who did not win the פייס. Their בגדי קודש were taken off because they had no עבודה to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: No, it is about those who did not win the lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects the proof. He says the משנה is about the losers, not the winners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone wore בגדי קודש during the פייס, the losers had to take them off afterward. So the משנה fits רב ששת's view just as well, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: No — signals that the proposed reading is being rejected
Who did not win

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said that Rav Sheshet said:
No, it is about those who did not win the lottery.
phrases.notes: Their sacred garments were removed because they were not doing any service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 1 by reassigning which group the משנה describes.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must be about the winners
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can just as easily describe the losers removing their בגדי קודש.

steps.title: Logic supports רב ששת's reading because trousers must go on first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רב ששת's reading makes more sense. If the משנה described the winners, the sacred מכנסים would be put on after the other garments. But a ברייתא learns from a פסוק that nothing may be put on before the מכנסים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is reasonable. For if you think it is about those who won the lottery, how could it say 'they left only the trousers on them'? But a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that nothing should come before the trousers? The verse says: 'And linen trousers shall be on his flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing support for רב ששת's reading. It shows that reading the משנה as describing the winners runs into a problem with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the winners kept their everyday מכנסים on, they would have to put the other בגדי קודש on top and only switch the מכנסים at the end. That would break the rule, learned from 'ומכנסי בד יהיו על בשרו', that the מכנסים come first. So the משנה reads more smoothly as describing the losers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So too it is logical' — introduces support for the previous answer
'For if it entered your mind…' — introduces a reading that leads to a problem
Trousers, one of the priestly garments
'The verse teaches' — introduces the פסוק that is the source

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable.
For if it would enter your mind
that it is about those who won the lottery,

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין עֲלֵיהֶן אֶלָּא מִכְנָסַיִם בִּלְבַד״?
phrases.english: how could it say 'they left on them only the trousers'?
phrases.notes: Those would be everyday trousers, and the sacred garments would go on top of them.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר קוֹדֶם לַמִּכְנָסַיִם —
phrases.english: But it was taught: From where do we know that nothing should come before the trousers?
The verse teaches:
'And linen trousers shall be on his flesh!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 by showing that the alternative reading conflicts with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's reading that the משנה describes the losers
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא based on 'ומכנסי בד יהיו על בשרו' requiring the מכנסים to be put on first
steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes the order of dressing in the בגדי כהונה: the מכנסים always come first.

steps.title: רב נחמן's side: the sacred trousers went on before the everyday clothes came off
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion (רב נחמן) answers that the winners put on the sacred מכנסים while still wearing their בגדי חול. Only afterward were the בגדי חול removed, so the מכנסים still came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? This is no difficulty. This is what it teaches: while the everyday clothes are still on them, they put the sacred trousers on them; then they remove the everyday clothes, leaving only the trousers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן would deal with the problem from step 3, and gives his answer. This defends the reading that the משנה describes the winners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the sacred מכנסים would come last. But if the sacred מכנסים were put on underneath before the בגדי חול were taken off, nothing sacred was worn before them. So the משנה can describe the winners after all, and the support for רב ששת is neutralized.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the other one?' — how does the other opinion answer this?
'This is not difficult'
'This is what it teaches' — reinterprets the source's wording
Everyday (non-sacred) clothes
Sacred priestly trousers

phrases.english: And the other one? This is not difficult,
this is what it teaches:
while the everyday clothes are still on them,
they dress them in the sacred trousers,
and then they would remove the everyday clothes from them,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶלָּא מִכְנָסַיִם בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: and they would leave only the trousers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 3 on behalf of רב נחמן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that reading the משנה as describing the winners breaks the dressing order
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sacred מכנסים could be put on under the בגדי חול first, so they still came before everything else.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be read either way, so it does not decide the מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רב ששת.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'trousers left on' in the משנה are the sacred מכנסים according to this answer, not everyday ones.

steps.title: רב ששת's own source: the lottery in לשכת הגזית
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא describing the פייס in לשכת הגזית. The כהנים stood in a circle, and the ממונה took the מצנפת off one כהן's head to mark where the count would begin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: From where do I say this? As it was taught in a ברייתא: לשכת הגזית was like a large basilica. The פייס was in its east, and a זקן sat in its west. The כהנים stood surrounding in a circle like a bracelet. The ממונה comes and takes the מצנפת off the head of one of them, and they know that the lottery count starts from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now brings his own proof that the כהנים wore בגדי קודש. This step presents the ברייתא, and the next step draws the conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the ממונה removed a מצנפת to mark the starting point of the count. The rest of the ברייתא describes the setting of the פייס.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do I say this?' — introduces the speaker's own source
The Chamber of Hewn Stone in the בית המקדש, where the פייס was held
A basilica, a large hall with pillars
A bracelet or ring shape (a circle)
The appointed officer in charge of the פייס
The priestly turban (mitre), one of the בגדי כהונה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say it? As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית כְּמִין בָּסִילְקֵי גְּדוֹלָה הָיְתָה,
phrases.english: The Chamber of Hewn Stone was like a large basilica;
the lottery was in its east, and an elder sat in its west.
phrases.notes: The elder was there to rule on any doubtful cases.

phrases.english: And the priests stood surrounding in a circle like a bracelet,
and the appointed one comes and takes the mitre
from the head of one of them,
and they know that the lottery count begins from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה turned out to be inconclusive, רב ששת brings an independent source for his view.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that the פייס was done in בגדי קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing the פייס in לשכת הגזית

steps.title: A mitre proves they wore sacred garments
steps.stepSummary: If the כהנים wore בגדי חול during the פייס, there would be no מצנפת to remove, because a מצנפת is a priestly garment. So they must have been in בגדי קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think they were in everyday clothes, is there such a thing as a mitre among everyday clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of רב ששת's proof from the ברייתא. The mention of a מצנפת shows the כהנים were dressed in בגדי קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצנפת belongs only to the בגדי כהונה, and no one wears one as everyday clothing. Since the ממונה removed a מצנפת during the פייס, the כהנים must have been wearing בגדי קודש, as רב ששת holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is there…?' — a rhetorical question expecting the answer 'no'
In everyday clothes

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind that they were in everyday clothes,
is there a mitre among everyday clothes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that the פייס was done in בגדי קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The detail of removing a מצנפת, which is a priestly garment
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's proof rests on the assumption that a מצנפת is only a priestly garment. The next step rejects that assumption, so the proof does not stand.

steps.title: A priestly-style hat can be a private, non-sacred garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב ששת's proof. A כהן can own a priestly-style garment that is not sacred, as shown by the teaching about a כתונת his mother made for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, such a thing exists. As רב יהודה taught (some say רב שמואל בר יהודה): A כהן whose mother made him a tunic may serve in it for an individual's עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof from step 6. A כהן could wear a privately made מצנפת as an ordinary weekday garment, so taking one off his head does not prove he was in בגדי קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 assumed that every מצנפת is a sacred garment. The teaching about the mother's כתונת shows that a כהן can own a priestly-style garment made privately, and it is not part of the community's בגדי קודש. So the ממונה may have removed a private מצנפת, and רב נחמן's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic)
Tunic, one of the priestly garments
A service for an individual's offering (not a communal one)

steps.confusionAlert: The mother's כתונת is not a garment of חול in the sense of being invalid. It is valid only for עבודת יחיד, not for communal service. The point here is only that priestly-style garments can be privately owned, so a מצנפת does not automatically mean בגדי קודש.

phrases.english: Yes —
phrases.notes: Yes, there can be a מצנפת that is not one of the sacred garments.

phrases.english: as Rav Yehuda taught
and some say Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda:
A priest whose mother made him a tunic,
may perform an individual's service in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the מצנפת in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove רב נחמן's view correct.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that every מצנפת is a sacred garment. A privately made priestly-style garment can exist.

steps.title: אביי learns two facts about לשכת הגזית
steps.stepSummary: אביי infers from the ברייתא that לשכת הגזית was half in קודש and half in חול, and that it had two doorways.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that לשכת הגזית was half in the holy area and half in the non-holy area. And learn that it had two doorways, one opening into the holy area and one opening into the non-holy area.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a side topic based on the ברייתא of step 5. He states two conclusions, and the next steps will prove each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the פייס happened in the east of the room and the זקן sat in the west. אביי sees a tension there and resolves it by describing how the building was laid out. This step only states his claims. The proofs follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this / conclude from it
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, where the סנהדרין sat
The holy (sanctified) area of the עזרה
The non-holy area, outside the sanctified courtyard
Doorways

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Learn from this that the Chamber of Hewn Stone
was half in the sacred area and half in the non-sacred area,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים הָיוּ לָהּ,
phrases.english: and learn from this that it had two doorways,
one opening into the sacred area,
and one opening into the non-sacred area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion that grows out of the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לשכת הגזית was half in קודש and half in חול, with one doorway to each side.

steps.title: The room was not entirely in the holy area
steps.stepSummary: If the whole room were in קודש, the זקן could not sit in its west, because only kings of the house of David may sit in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the whole room was in the holy area, how could the elder sit in its west? But the master said: No one may sit in the עזרה except kings of the house of David alone.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves his first claim by ruling out one option. The room cannot be entirely in קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a זקן sat in the west part of the room. Sitting in the עזרה is forbidden to everyone except kings from בית דוד. So the west part where he sat must have been in חול.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it should enter your mind (if you assume)
An elder (here, the one who sat in the chamber)
There is no sitting in the Temple courtyard
Kings of the house of David

phrases.english: For if you think it was entirely in the sacred area —
would an elder sit in its west?
But the master said:
There is no sitting in the courtyard
except for kings of the house of David alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving אביי's first claim from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That part of the room (the west) was in חול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that only kings of בית דוד may sit in the עזרה, together with the ברייתא's statement that the זקן sat in the west.

steps.title: The room was not entirely in the non-holy area
steps.stepSummary: If the whole room were in חול, the פייס could not take place in its east, because the פייס must happen in the בית אלהים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the whole room was in the non-holy area, how could the lottery be held in its east? We need 'In the house of God we walk with the throng,' and that would be missing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rules out the opposite option. The room cannot be entirely in חול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the גמרא, the פסוק 'בבית אלהים נהלך ברגש' was used to show that the excited crowd of the פייס belongs inside the holy area. So the east part, where the פייס was held, must have been in קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery that assigned the Temple services
We require
With a throng / with commotion
And there is not (that would be missing)

phrases.english: And if you think it was entirely in the non-sacred area —
would the lottery be in its east?
But we require
"In the House of God we walk with the throng,"
and that would be missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 9: it rules out the opposite option.
steps.raayaObject: That part of the room (the east) was in קודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק בבית אלהים נהלך ברגש, together with the ברייתא's statement that the פייס was held in the east.

steps.title: Conclusion: the room was half holy and half non-holy
steps.stepSummary: Since the room was neither entirely in קודש nor entirely in חול, it must have been half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: half of it was in the holy area and half in the non-holy area.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes his first proof. The room was split between the holy and non-holy areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 ruled out 'all קודש' and step 10 ruled out 'all חול,' so only 'half and half' is left. The east side was holy for the פייס, and the west side was חול for the sitting זקן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the only remaining option)
Half of it

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
half was in the sacred area and half in the non-sacred area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: חֶצְיָהּ בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in steps 9 and 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לשכת הגזית was half in קודש (east) and half in חול (west).

steps.title: It could not have had only one door opening to the holy side
steps.stepSummary: A room whose only door opens into קודש counts entirely as קודש. Then the זקן could not sit in its west.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it had one door opening to the holy area, how could the elder sit in its west? But we learned in a משנה: Chambers built in the non-holy area but opening into the holy area, their inside is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now begins proving his second claim, about the two doorways. He rules out a single door that opens toward קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה teaches that the door decides the status of the whole room. A room that opens into קודש is entirely holy, even the part built on חול ground. Then the west side would also be holy, and the זקן could not sit there.

keyTerms.meaning: Doorway
Chambers / rooms in the Temple complex
Their interior

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that the ground under a room decides its status. Here the doorway decides it. That is why proving the room was half and half is not enough, and אביי still needs two doors.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ פֶּתַח אֶחָד יֵשׁ לָהּ
phrases.english: And if you think it had one doorway
opening to the sacred area —
would an elder sit in its west?
But we learned in a mishna:
Chambers built in the non-sacred area
and opening into the sacred area —
their interior is sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ פֶּתַח אֶחָד יֵשׁ לָהּ וּפָתוּחַ לַקּוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the location of the room to the question of its doorways.
steps.raayaObject: The room did not have a single door opening only to קודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: rooms built in חול that open to קודש have a holy interior.

steps.title: It could not have had only one door opening to the non-holy side
steps.stepSummary: A room whose only door opens into חול counts entirely as חול. Then the פייס could not happen in its east.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think its door opened to the non-holy area, how could the lottery be held in its east? But we learned in a משנה: Chambers built in the holy area but opening into the non-holy area, their inside is non-holy.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rules out the opposite single-door option. One door toward חול does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the same משנה, a room that opens into חול is entirely חול, even the part built on holy ground. Then the east side, where the פייס was held, would not be holy, and the פייס would not be בבית אלהים.

keyTerms.meaning: Built (located)
Opening into

phrases.english: And if you think it opened to the non-sacred area —
would the lottery be in its east?
But we learned in a mishna:
Chambers built in the sacred area and opening into the non-sacred area —
their interior is non-sacred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The room did not have a single door opening only to חול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: rooms built in קודש that open to חול have a non-holy interior.

steps.title: Conclusion: the room had two doorways
steps.stepSummary: Since one door in either direction fails, the room must have had two doors, one to קודש and one to חול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that it had two doorways, one opening into the holy area and one opening into the non-holy area?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes his second proof and confirms his original statement from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a door on each side, each half keeps its own status. The east half opens to קודש and is holy, so the פייס is valid there. The west half opens to חול and is not holy, so the זקן may sit there.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that (introduces a firm conclusion)
Two doorways

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, לשכת הגזית stood half in קודש (east, where the פייס was held) and half in חול (west, where the זקן sat), with a door to each side. Both details are needed because the door, not just the ground, decides a room's status.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general rule about Temple chambers: the direction of the doorway sets the status of the space. This explains how holy and non-holy activities could happen in one building.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that we learn from this:
it had two doorways,
one opening into the sacred area
and one opening into the non-sacred area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים הָיוּ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof of steps 12 and 13 and confirms אביי's statement in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לשכת הגזית had two doorways, one to קודש and one to חול, so each half kept its own status.

steps.title: The jobs decided by the second lottery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the jobs assigned by the second פייס: slaughtering, sprinkling, clearing the inner מזבח, clearing the מנורה, and bringing the limbs to the כבש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second פייס decided: who slaughters, who sprinkles the blood, who cleans the ashes off the inner מזבח, who cleans the מנורה, and who brings the limbs up to the כבש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which jobs the second daily פייס handed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פייס only decided who would clear the outer מזבח. The second פייס covers the main jobs of the morning תמיד, from slaughtering it to carrying its pieces to the ramp of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughters the animal
Sprinkles the blood on the altar
Removes the ashes
The inner (golden) altar for incense
The ramp leading up to the outer altar

phrases.english: MISHNA: The second lottery:
who slaughters, who sprinkles,
who removes the ashes from the inner altar,
and who removes the ashes from the menorah,
and who brings the limbs up to the ramp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the לשכת הגזית room ended in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second פייס assigns slaughtering, sprinkling, clearing the inner מזבח, clearing the מנורה, and carrying the limbs to the כבש.

steps.title: How the limbs were split among thirteen priests
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the pieces of the תמיד and its accompanying offerings that were carried to the ramp, and totals thirteen כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The head and the right leg; the two front legs; the tail and the left leg; the chest and the throat; the two sides; the innards; the flour, the חביתין, and the wine. Thirteen priests won in this lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains exactly which pieces were carried and by whom. It ends by counting thirteen כהנים in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine כהנים carried items: six for the animal's pieces and three for the flour, the חביתין and the wine. Add the four jobs from step 15 (slaughter, sprinkle, inner מזבח, מנורה) and you get thirteen.

keyTerms.meaning: The tail end, including the fat tail
The throat/windpipe area
The two flanks (sides of the animal)
The intestines
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count only the carried items. The thirteen also includes the four jobs from the previous line, which were not carrying jobs.

phrases.english: The head and the leg, and the two forelegs,
the tail and the leg, and the breast and the throat,
and the two flanks, and the intestines.
And the fine flour, and the griddle-cakes, and the wine.
Thirteen priests won in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the last job of step 15 (carrying the limbs) and gives the total.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The limbs, flour, חביתין and wine are split among nine carriers, which makes thirteen כהנים for the second פייס.

steps.title: בן עזאי: the order follows how the animal walks
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי, quoting רבי יהושע, says the limbs were brought in the order of the animal's walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said before רבי עקיבא in the name of רבי יהושע: it was brought in the order in which it walks.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion about the order of the limbs is added to the משנה. The details will be explained later in the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה gave a set order for the pieces. בן עזאי says the order was different: it matched the way the animal moves when alive. The גמרא later spells out exactly what that order is.

keyTerms.meaning: The way it walks
Was offered/brought
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Ben Azzai said before Rabbi Akiva
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
It was offered in the way it walks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different order for the pieces listed in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן עזאי, the limbs were brought in the order the animal walks.

steps.title: One lottery for all the jobs, or one for each job?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the כהנים held one lottery for all thirteen jobs or a separate lottery for each job.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when they held the lottery, did they hold it for one job, or perhaps for each and every job?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about how the second פייס actually worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: they drew once for one job, and the winner's neighbors automatically got the other twelve jobs. Option two: they held a separate draw for each of the thirteen jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
They conduct a lottery
Or perhaps
A Temple service/job

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
When they conduct the lottery —
do they conduct it for one service,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא — לְכׇל עֲבוֹדָה וַעֲבוֹדָה הֵן מְפַיְּיסִין?
phrases.english: or perhaps they conduct it for each and every service?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the thirteen jobs from the משנה were assigned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was there one draw for all thirteen jobs, or a separate draw for each job?

steps.title: Proof from 'there were four lotteries'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove there was one draw only. The משנה says there were four פייסות in total, and separate draws would make many more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: there were four lotteries there. If you think they held a lottery for each job, there would be many!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by quoting an earlier משנה that counts four lotteries a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each of the thirteen jobs had its own draw, the second פייס alone would be thirteen lotteries. The total would then be far more than four. So it seems there was only one draw for the whole group.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind
Many

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַרְבַּע פְּיָיסוֹת הָיוּ שָׁם.
phrases.english: Come and hear: There were four lotteries there.
And if it would enter your mind
that they conduct a lottery for each service —
there would be many!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַרְבַּע פְּיָיסוֹת הָיוּ שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That there was one draw for all thirteen jobs
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's statement that there were four פייסות

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: four gatherings, many draws
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. 'Four' means four gatherings, and each gathering could include many separate draws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: this is what it means. They gathered four times for the lottery, and at each gathering there were many lotteries.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is pushed away by reading the word 'four' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'four' could count the times the כהנים came together for a lottery, not the number of draws. Each gathering could include many draws, so the question from step 18 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Gather to conduct the lottery
Each and every one

steps.whatToRemember: The statement 'four פייסות' cannot settle the question. It may count four gatherings, each with many separate draws.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: This is what it is saying:
Four times they gather to conduct the lottery,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְכׇל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא הָיוּ בַּהּ טוּבָא פְּיָיסוֹת.
phrases.english: and in each and every one there were many lotteries.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the original question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'four פייסות' means four draws. It can also mean four gatherings, each with many draws.
